title: Gate recordInboundMail on evidence.add and project staffing

approvals.evidence: Architect approval stated in the Claude Code session ("Approved", 2026-09-06), following the plan presentation for the recordInboundMail authorization bypass fix. Touches lib/workspace.ts (protected: adding a case to projectScopeOf, additive only); no migration.

body.design_ref: None -- no open design question; the fix mirrors an existing, working pattern (app/api/documents/route.ts's can() check) rather than introducing a new one.

steps.title: Add case 'recordInboundMail': return one(a.issueId) to projectScopeOf in lib/workspace.ts, beside the existing addEvidence/addNote/etc. cases it already resembles (same one-issue-id shape).
steps.verify_command: npx tsc --noEmit && npx tsx -e "import('./lib/workspace.ts').then(async m=>{const {initWorkspace}=m as any; })" ; npm run validate:scenarios

steps.title: In app/api/mail/file/route.ts, after loading state (so state.model is available) and before either mode branch, check can(state.model, session.actor, 'evidence.add'); return 403 with a clear message on refusal. Import can from '@/lib/access'.

In the attach-mode branch (after resolving target and confirming it exists), check the actor is staffed on target's project the same way app/api/workspace/route.ts does (isStaffedOn / the equivalent helper already imported there), returning 403 on refusal, before calling persistActions.

Add scenario(s) to scripts/scenario-validation.ts (module-level test, following the CD-prefix style already used for the client-filter work, or a new short prefix for this fix) proving AC1-AC5: no permission -> refused on both modes; permission but not staffed -> refused on attach; permission and staffed -> succeeds unchanged; a bare recordInboundMail action through apply() with no staffing -> refused by projectScopeOf directly, independent of the route.

commit_boundaries: Steps 1 and 4 together: the reducer's own staffing gate and the scenario proving it are one unit -- a gate nothing proves is a hope, not a gate.

Steps 2 and 3 together, as their own commit: the route-level permission and staffing checks. Kept separate from step 1's commit because the route fix alone already closes the vulnerability end to end; the reducer-level gate is defense in depth and reverts independently if it ever needs to.
body.rollback: Revert the route-level commit (steps 2+3) alone reopens the route to any signed-in user again, so it should only be reverted alongside re-disabling the endpoint entirely, not on its own. Revert the reducer commit (steps 1+4) alone is always safe: it only adds a new refusal path for an action type nothing else currently constructs through a legitimate channel other than this route and the machine intake path (which never carries a human actor and is unaffected).
